=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The path diagnostic applies only security_audit_sanitize_log_value to lines matching ENOENT/os error 2/No such file or directory, bypassing security_audit_mask_stderr_line entirely. When a path-error line also contains a secret-named env value (e.g. provider failed: No such file or directory: k3y9 with SHORT_API_KEY=k3y9), the secret value reaches captured_path_error= unmasked, before the masked tail ever runs.
  WHY: The old sanitizer (lines 25-38) only masks url userinfo, Authorization/Bearer headers, ghp_ tokens, and sk-or- keys. It does not mask arbitrary env values (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GH_TOKEN, short secrets), sk-proj-/sk-ant- keys, long hex runs, or long base64 runs. The round-2 commit added security_audit_mask_stderr_line to cover those gaps but applied it only inside security_audit_emit_codex_stderr_tail, leaving the pre-existing path diagnostic as a bypass that prints selected stderr lines with the old sanitizer only.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The raw stderr, env values, and the Codex config are never printed." (PR description checklist item 5)
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh, security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic at lines 65-73 — needs to apply security_audit_mask_stderr_line to the diagnostic output before security_audit_sanitize_log_value; tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py — a regression test feeding a stderr line that matches the path-error regex AND contains a secret-named env value, asserting the value is absent from captured_path_error=
  Evidence of absence: The diff adds security_audit_mask_stderr_line and applies it only inside security_audit_emit_codex_stderr_tail at line 211. security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic at lines 65-73 is unchanged by the PR. No diff hunk adds the masking pass to the path diagnostic. No test exercises a secret and path-error pattern on the same stderr line: the existing test at line 986 uses separate lines for secrets and os error 2, and no new test covers the co-occurrence case. Copilot review comment entry[12] explicitly asked for both the mask pass and the regression test; neither is in the current diff.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The path diagnostic reads Codex stderr and passes the matched lines through `security_audit_sanitize_log_value` only, bypassing the new `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` helper. The call site at line 1341 runs BEFORE the masked tail at line 1342, so a secret-named environment value on a path-error line is emitted unmasked via `captured_path_error=`. The Copilot review comment entry[12] (line 1342) cites a concrete repro: `provider failed: k3y9 No such file or directory` with `SHORT_API_KEY=k3y9` prints `captured_path_error=...k3y9...`. The round-2 fixes only updated `security_audit_emit_codex_stderr_tail`; `security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic` was untouched, so the documented guarantee in agents.md §7 ("`sk-` keys, long hex and base64 runs (either alphabet, padded or not), and the values of secret-named env vars ... are masked") and in the changelog fragment ("the values of secret-named env vars are masked") is violated for any codex stderr where the secret and the path-error pattern share one line.
  WHY: Codex can produce lines like `provider failed: <token> No such file or directory` (for example a libcurl or sandbox helper echoing the API key with an ENOENT). `grep -E '(No such file or directory|os error 2|ENOENT)'` selects the line; `security_audit_sanitize_log_value` only masks Bearer/Authorization/ghp_/URL userinfo, not arbitrary env values; the secret value reaches the GitHub Actions log.
- Review note: scripts/security_audit.sh, line 98, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in *TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*|PAT|*_PAT|PAT_*|*_PAT_*)` arm of `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The bare `PAT` alternative is a literal-name match, not a substring match; the round-1 rejection is correct and no change is needed.
  WHY: Direct shell test (verified 2026-10-01): `PAT` is a literal-name match in `[[ pattern = pattern ]]`, so `PATH`, `PATTERN`, `COMPAT`, etc. fall through to `*) continue`.
- Review note: scripts/security_audit.sh, line 130 of `security_audit_mask_stderr_line`, the sed chain `s#[[:alnum:]+/_-]{40,}={0,2}#[redacted]#g` | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The combined class covers both base64 alphabets plus optional padding and is correct in principle; no regression was observed.
  WHY: The round-2 fix closes the unpadded `/`-bearing gap, and `test_security_audit_codex_stderr_tail_masks_short_secrets_and_unpadded_base64` covers unpadded standard and split cases.
- scripts/security_audit.sh, `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` short-value branch at lines 112-127 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For a short secret value <8 chars, the whole-word branch does not replace an occurrence when a neighbour is in `[[:alnum:]_-]`, so a secret on the boundary of a longer token (e.g. `prefix-k3y9-suffix` where `k3y9` is the value) is not masked.
  WHY: A JWT-shaped or cookie-style string containing a short secret token between hyphens can pass through to the Actions log. The round-2 design (AD-8) explicitly traded this off to avoid mangling digits inside words/ids; the reviewer describes this as a known limitation, not a fix recommendation.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The raw stderr, env values, and the Codex config are never printed." (PR description checklist item 5; restated in agents.md §7 note at line 2175 and changelog fragment at line 5: "Every line is masked for `sk-` keys, long hex and base64 runs (standard or URL-safe, padded or not), and the values of secret-named env vars (short values where they stand as a whole word), then passed through the existing log sanitizer.")
  Expected change site: `scripts/security_audit.sh` `security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic` (lines 65-73) — pipe each selected path-diagnostic line through `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` before `security_audit_sanitize_log_value`; `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py` — a regression test that feeds a stderr line where a secret-named env var value and a path-error pattern co-occur on the same line (e.g. `provider failed: k3y9 No such file or directory` with `SHORT_API_KEY=k3y9`) and asserts the value does not appear in `captured_path_error=`.
  Evidence of absence: The diff introduces `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` (line 87) and applies it only inside `security_audit_emit_codex_stderr_tail` at line 211. `security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic` (lines 65-73) is unchanged and calls only `security_audit_sanitize_log_value` at line 71. The codex-execution call sequence at lines 1341-1342 invokes the path diagnostic before the masked tail. No test feeds a stderr line where the secret and the path-error regex pattern co-occur on one line; the existing `test_security_audit_codex_failure_preserves_status_and_reports_context` (lines 967-990) keeps them on separate lines and asserts only the long secret values (which the older sanitizer already covered). The Copilot review comment entry[12] on line 1342 explicitly identifies this as a regression of the no-env-value guarantee and asks for both the mask pass and a regression test, neither of which is in the current diff.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
